facts: The instantaneous rate of change at $x = c$ is $f'(c)$, the gradient of the tangent line at $x = c$.
Read the two points off the **tangent line**, not off the curve.
State the rate with compound units, such as $\text{m/s}$, $^{\circ}\text{C/min}$ or $\text{L/s}$.
Hand-drawn tangents vary slightly, so a graph estimate is only close to the true gradient.
steps: Locate the specified point $P(c, f(c))$ on the curve and inspect the drawn tangent line.
Select two points $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$ that lie clearly on the tangent line at grid intersections.
State the instantaneous rate of change with the appropriate physical units.

foundation.solution_text:
Choose two points on the tangent line: $(0, 0)$ and $(4, 8)$.
$f'(2) = \dfrac{8 - 0}{4 - 0}$
$= \dfrac{8}{4}$
$= 2$

Read two points on the tangent line: $(0, 70)$ and $(30, 10)$.
$T'(10) = \dfrac{10 - 70}{30 - 0}$
$= \dfrac{-60}{30}$
$= -2^{\circ}\text{C/min}$

$\text{Tangent } T_1\text{ at } x = 1\text{ has gradient } m \approx 0.5.$
$\text{Tangent } T_2\text{ at } x = 4\text{ has gradient } m \approx 2.$
$\text{The instantaneous rate of change at } x = 4\text{ is greater than at } x = 1\text{ } (2 > 0.5).$

Using points $(0, -1)$ and $(2, 3)$ on the tangent line:
$f'(1) = \dfrac{3 - (-1)}{2 - 0}$
$= \dfrac{4}{2}$
$= 2$

Use the points $(2, 10)$ and $(6, 50)$ on the tangent line:
$\text{Instantaneous speed} = \dfrac{50 - 10}{6 - 2}$
$= \dfrac{40}{4}$
$= 10\text{ m/s}$

foundation.question_text: When estimating the instantaneous rate of change at point $P(2, 4)$ on a curve, why must the two points used for the gradient calculation lie on the tangent line rather than elsewhere on the curve?
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{The instantaneous rate of change is the gradient of the tangent line.}$
$\text{Points on the curve other than } P\text{ form a secant chord, whereas points along the tangent line give its straight-line slope.}$

development.question_text: A population curve $P(t)$ has tangents drawn at $t = 2\text{ years}$ (gradient $m_1 = 40$) and at $t = 6\text{ years}$ (gradient $m_2 = 150$). Describe how the rate of population growth is changing over time.
development.solution_text:
$\text{At } t = 2\text{, the instantaneous growth rate is } 40\text{ individuals/year}.$
$\text{At } t = 6\text{, the instantaneous growth rate is } 150\text{ individuals/year}.$
$\text{The instantaneous rate of population growth is increasing rapidly over time (accelerating growth).}$

A tangent line drawn to a curve at point $P$ crosses the $y$-axis at $(0, 12)$ and the $x$-axis at $(6, 0)$. Calculate the gradient of this tangent line.

The concentration $C(t)$ of a medication in $\text{mg/L}$ after $t$ hours is graphed. The tangent line drawn at $t = 3\text{ h}$ passes through $(1, 8)$ and $(5, 2)$. Estimate the instantaneous rate of change in concentration at $t = 3\text{ hours}$.

mastery.question_text: A water heating experiment has temperature $T(t)$ graphed over $20\text{ minutes}$. The tangent line at $t = 10\text{ min}$ passes through $(4, 30)$ and $(16, 78)$, while the average rate over the entire $[0, 20]$ interval is $3.2^{\circ}\text{C/min}$. Calculate the instantaneous rate at $t = 10\text{ min}$ and compare it with the overall average rate.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Instantaneous rate: } T'(10) = \dfrac{78 - 30}{16 - 4} = \dfrac{48}{12} = 4^{\circ}\text{C/min}$
$\text{Overall average rate} = 3.2^{\circ}\text{C/min}$
$\text{The instantaneous rate at } t = 10\text{ min } (4^{\circ}\text{C/min})\text{ is greater than the overall average rate } (3.2^{\circ}\text{C/min}).$

$\text{At local extrema } x = -2\text{ and } x = 3\text{, the tangent lines are horizontal, so } f'(-2) = 0\text{ and } f'(3) = 0.$
$\text{Between the local maximum at } x = -2\text{ and the local minimum at } x = 3\text{, the curve is decreasing, so } f'(0) < 0\text{ (negative).}$

mastery.question_text: A high-resolution graph of $y = f(x)$ shows a tangent line at $(4, 8)$ that passes through $(1, 2)$ and $(7, 14)$. Calculate $f'(4)$, determine the equation of this tangent line in the form $y = mx + c$, and find its $x$-intercept.
mastery.solution_text:
$m = \dfrac{14 - 2}{7 - 1} = \dfrac{12}{6} = 2 \implies f'(4) = 2$
$y - 8 = 2(x - 4) \implies y = 2x$
$\text{Setting } y = 0 \implies 2x = 0 \implies x = 0$
$\text{Equation: } y = 2x, \quad x\text{-intercept: } (0, 0)$
